Definition: to tumble (in ruins); figuratively, to perish
BiblicalUsage: Makak means to tumble down, to decay, to be brought low, and its three appearances all show the same fall. Ecclesiastes 10:18 says by much slothfulness the building decayeth and the house droppeth through, and Job 24:24 says the wicked are exalted for a little while but are gone and brought low. Psalms 106:43 says Israel was brought low for their iniquity, though God delivered them many times.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe this word is a warning against both laziness and pride: the slothful house in Ecclesiastes 10:18 and the exalted wicked in Job 24:24 fall the same way. My position is that Psalms 106:43 is the hope inside it, because the people brought low were delivered many times, and God still delivers.
